name: Motion Film
description: Design and render a motion-design film in code — launch videos, promos, feature announcements, explainers, brand openers, social loops — as one time-seeked HTML file rendered to MP4 with Playwright + ffmpeg.
prompt:
# Motion Film

Use this skill when the user wants a motion-design film made in code: launch video, product promo, feature announcement, animated explainer, brand/event opener, social loop, or keynote-style film.

Do not use this skill when:
- the user wants a reusable editor app (use `motion-editor`)
- the request is a Manim math/algorithm explainer (use `manim-video`)
- the user is working in a HyperFrames composition (use `hyperframes`)
- the task is editing existing live-action footage or generating a clip with a video model

Inputs:
- Project brief: {{project_brief}}
- Film kind: {{film_kind}}
- Aspect: {{aspect}}
- Length seconds: {{length_seconds}}
- Output dir: {{output_dir}}

Workflow:
1. Resolve the project folder. If `{{output_dir}}` is empty, use `motion-film-project` in the current workspace.
2. Read `{baseDir}/SKILL.md`, `{baseDir}/references/techniques.md` and `{baseDir}/references/taste.md` before designing. Use `{baseDir}/references/example-launch-film.md` as the quality and density bar, not as a script. If the idea is a simulation (agents, particles, a 3D machine or fly-through), also read `{baseDir}/references/sims.md` and follow simulation mode.
3. Brief: ask once for what is missing (project, kind, format, brand, assets, music, style), offering the SKILL.md defaults so the user can answer "defaults". If a music track is supplied, find its tempo, downbeats and drop with `python3 {baseDir}/scripts/beats.py <track> --duration <length> -o beats.json` instead of asking for them. Use only user-supplied or free-for-commercial-use assets; never invent product UI the user did not ask for.
4. Design: write the story as 4-6 acts chained by transforms, put every beat in `timeline.json` (named timestamps in seconds, grouped by act) and the same as a beat map table (beat, time, trigger, transform, SFX), budget reading holds for every line of text, and render 3-5 stills from a stub `seek(t)`. Stop and get approval before the full build.
5. Build one HTML file at target resolution where every style is computed inside `async seek(t)` and every time comes from `timeline.json`: no CSS transitions/animations, timers, `Date.now()`, unseeded randomness, carried state, or hardcoded start times. Use closed-form springs and the numbers in taste.md. One continuous take; no crossfades, blur-ins, 3D flips or empty frames; particles and glows only in simulation mode. Every readable state holds at least 1s (plus ~0.25s per word beyond three, at least 2s for the final line) and text never moves while it is being read.
6. Sound (read `{baseDir}/references/sound.md`): downloaded SFX positioned by measured peak, or generated with the bundled engine from a cue sheet that reads `timeline.json` (`PYTHONPATH={baseDir}/scripts python3 -m sfx cues.py`); song starting on a downbeat; final mix at -14 LUFS. Skip if the user wants silent.
7. Review loop (read `{baseDir}/references/review-loop.md`): render half-resolution drafts, build contact sheets at every beat with `node {baseDir}/scripts/sheet.mjs --video draft.mp4`, open them, check the checklist, fix and repeat until a full pass is clean. Then render with Playwright (4 subframes per frame) and ffmpeg `tmix` to 60fps motion blur, sheet the final file, scan for single-frame pops (frame-diff spikes 3x neighbours), fix and re-render, mux audio, and check it with `node {baseDir}/scripts/wave.mjs film.mp4`.
8. Write run artifacts to:
   - `{artifactDir}/beat-map.md`
   - `{artifactDir}/render-report.md`
   Include acts, beats, assets and licenses, render command, the contact sheets reviewed, what each review pass fixed, and pop and loudness results.
9. End with the exact MP4 path, a few representative frames, and any missing dependencies (Node, Playwright Chromium, ffmpeg, Python 3).

Success criteria:
- Stills and beat map approved before the full build.
- The film is deterministic, seekable, reads every time from `timeline.json`, and passes a clean review-loop pass plus the pop check.
- The delivered MP4 matches the requested format, length, and loop behaviour.

parameters.name: project_brief
parameters.description: What the project is, who it's for, and the one thing the viewer should remember

routing.useWhen: Use when the user asks to make a launch video, product promo, feature announcement, motion graphics, animated explainer, brand or event opener, social loop, keynote-style film, a simulation-style video (agents, particles, a 3D fly-through), or to make a video with code.
routing.dontUseWhen: Do not use for building a reusable motion editor app (use motion-editor), Manim math or algorithm explainers (use manim-video), HyperFrames compositions (use hyperframes), editing existing live-action footage, or model-generated video clips.
routing.outputs: A time-seeked HTML film, timeline.json, render script, approved beat map and stills, contact sheets, optional cue sheet, and a muxed MP4 in the project folder, plus beat-map and render-report artifacts under {artifactDir}.
routing.successCriteria: Stills and beat map approved before the build; the film is deterministic, seekable and timed from timeline.json; reading holds respected; a full contact-sheet review pass and the single-frame pop check are clean; the MP4 matches the requested format and length.
